**Hover is an expand, not a restyle** — heights grow: Home 489→522, PLP/PDP 522→541, Wishlist 546→565; Home with Unavailable=True 489→570.

## Findings that MUST shape the plan

1. **`overrides/app/components/product-tile/` DOES NOT EXIST.** Neither does `CardBaseline` — it appears only as prose in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` lines 128/181/186. Nothing to extend.
2. **DO NOT create `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`.** The overrides resolver would silently redirect PLP, Search, Home, Cart, PDP and empty-search-results to it. `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-list/index.jsx:51-53` does `import ProductTile, {Skeleton as ProductTileSkeleton}` — an override without a named `Skeleton` export **breaks PLP at import time**. Build in `ui-kits/` instead; blast radius is then only explicit importers.
3. **The recipe key cannot be `ProductTile`** — `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts:357` fails any recipe shadowing a base SFCC recipe name. Use a `Zimm`-prefixed key.
4. **Reuse these existing registered atoms** rather than rebuilding: `zimmProductName`, `zimmProductPrice`, `zimmProductDescription`, `zimmColourSwatch`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup`, `zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`. All under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/`.
5. **Pattern to match: PR #64** (SFCC-89) — 5 atoms + 2 molecules, four-file set each (`index.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`, `<name>.css.ts`), recipe registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.
6. **Exemplar to copy precisely: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/`.** Named export (PascalCase) always; default export only if a consumer needs `React.lazy`. Props type declared inline at top, named `<Component>Props`, not exported; exported data types go alongside. Recipe key is a module-level const, consumed via `useMultiStyleConfig(KEY, props)`. Parts applied with `<chakra.div __css={styles.x}>` — `__css`, not `sx`, and `chakra.*` primitives not `Box`/`Flex`. i18n via `defineMessages` at module scope + `useIntl()`.
7. **Recipe rules:** `<name>.css.ts` exports a named const matching the recipe key exactly, with `parts: [...]` and a `baseStyle` function of the props. Values must be `var(--zimm-*)` custom properties — **bare Chakra token keys fail `recipeGuards.test.ts`**. Responsive steps are **explicit media queries keyed off a `BP` const**, never Chakra's array shorthand (the guard walks arrays and fails every element). `recipeParts.test.ts` fails if any `styles.X` read in `index.tsx` is missing from `parts`.
8. **Tests:** Vitest + RTL. Mock `useMultiStyleConfig` to return a flat parts object. Mock the icons barrel (`vi.mock('.../zimmIcon')`) — it has a Vitest SVG side-effect failure. **`useIntl` throws without a provider** — wrap renders in `IntlProvider` + `MemoryRouter`.
9. **No data fetching inside `overrides/app/components/`** — the card receives everything as props. `useIntl`/`useUiCopy` are the only permitted exceptions.
10. **Interactions are OUT of scope.** Add-to-bag and size-selection behaviour belong to SFCC-185 (PLP Quick Add), SFCC-497 (Wishlist Add to Bag), SFCC-90 (Homepage) — confirmed by the reporter in Jira comment 13812. The card renders the controls; the wiring lands elsewhere. Design for that: controls should be render-slot / callback-prop driven.
11. **Page wiring is OUT of scope.** PLP, Cart and Wishlist have no page override at all (base-only) and base Wishlist renders `ProductItem`, a row. Do not plan page ports.

## Verified requirement corrections (do not re-litigate)
- **It is a BAG icon, not a wishlist star.** Verified in Figma (`Icon_bag`); `atom/add-to-wishlist` is not placed in any card variant. SPR-14/SPR-15 were amended wishlist→cart. CRM-113–119 still says star but is stale.
- **SPR-05 (model/item view toggle) is struck through** — descoped, do not implement.
- **SPR-16 reads "~~clickable~~ product badges"** — badges are display-only, not clickable.
- **SPR-11:** each colour variant renders as a separate tile.
- **PRC-09/17/18:** the price slot needs three states plus precedence — list, sale (Was/Now), and customer-group/VIC, where "customer group discounts prevail over sale pricing". Treat VIC as a flagged assumption (ties to SFCC-778, currently blocked by this story).

## Assumptions to state explicitly in the plan
- "Recently Viewed Full History" variation = Figma `Type=PLP/PDP` (the AC says "same behavior as PLP card"). No fifth variant designed or built.
- `Hero` size / `Type=Defualt` is out of scope — no AC covers it, and its two variants have byte-identical names (a Figma variant conflict).
- **No Tablet card variant exists.** Artboards are 402 / 768 / 1440; 769–1439 is unspecified and Chakra's `md` is 768. The plan must state which side of 768 the mobile/desktop variants serve.
- The AC says hover reveals **arrows** to page through images; Figma ships `Slide indicator`, a dot/bar indicator, not arrows. Flag; do not silently pick one.
- Badge rendering: `.docs/prd/plp.md:71` says badges are not yet in PLP designs, and TSD-SFCC-225 delivers `c_productBadges` only on the product **GET** hook — PLP/search grids come from product *search*, so the attribute will not be in tile data. Treat the badge slot as present-but-unfed.
- No loading state and no empty state exist in the Figma set.

## Tier / ownership constraints
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**` — CODEOWNERS: `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b`, no approver teams.
- `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` — squads only (last-match-wins rule).
- **`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` is Tier 2, UI-Designer + tier-2 + tier-1 approvers — unavoidable, every new recipe registers there.** Flag it as the one Tier 2 touch.
- Do NOT touch `overrides/app/theme/foundation/**` or `theme/index.ts` (Tier 1). If a value has no existing `--zimm-*` token, say so and leave it — do not invent one.
- AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10: crossing protection tiers needs scope confirmation.

## House rules
TypeScript only under `overrides/`. Australian spelling in Zimmermann-authored identifiers. `textStyle` for type, never raw `fontSize`. Storybook story required, `title: 'Commerce/...'`, mandatory `Default` export. `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass. WCAG 2.2 AA (note: Figma's `touchContainer` is exactly 24×24 — meets SC 2.5.8 with zero margin).

## Deliverable
Goal statement · scale call (multi-commit or multi-branch, with reasoning — note the branch must be cut fresh from `develop`; the current checked-out branch is a merged SFCC-91 branch) · file manifest with tier and owner per file · sequenced steps each with concrete, checkable pass criteria · per-step loop configuration · open questions. Be specific about component decomposition: which atoms/molecules, and whether the variation axis is a config prop or a discriminated union (note the Wishlist type needs printed colour+size and a remove CTA that the others don't).

content.text:
# Plan ready — SFCC-236

**One branch, seven commits, one PR.** 21 new files + 3 modified. Full build loop per step, because eight tickets are blocked on this prop contract.

```bash
git fetch origin && git checkout -b feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component origin/develop
```

## Component shape

Six new ui-kits components — one organism, four molecules, one atom:

| | |
|---|---|
| `organisms/zimmProductCard` | the card; owns all hover rules |
| `molecules/zimmProductCardMedia` | image stack, arrows, paging |
| `molecules/zimmProductCardContent` | name, bag icon, attributes, price, size slot |
| `molecules/zimmSizeSelector` + `atoms/zimmSizeSelectorOption` | mirrors the colour-swatch pair |
| `molecules/zimmSlideIndicator` | the dot/bar strip |

Reusing `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmIcon` — no new icons needed, `bag`/`close`/`chevron-*` all exist.

## Three calls worth your eye

**The variation axis is a discriminated union, not a style string.** The ticket says "style prop", but the ACs won't survive one: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + a mandatory `onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist card with no remove CTA. The extensibility AC is then satisfied by a `VARIATION_CONFIG` table — add a union member and a config row, touch no JSX. There's a test that `index.tsx` contains no `switch` on `variation`.

**Hover is CSS-only, on `:hover, :focus-within`.** React hover state means 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer move — a PLP perf defect. `:focus-within` isn't optional either: WCAG 2.2 AA needs the revealed size selector keyboard-reachable. And every hover rule is gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` so a 768px touch tablet doesn't get hover-only content.

**One `<a>` per card, stretched-link.** The card holds a bag button, arrows, size options and a remove button — nesting those inside an anchor is invalid HTML. Link wraps the name only, with an `::after` overlay.

## Tier exposure

**Exactly one Tier 2 file:** `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — six append-only registrations. Everything else is `ui-kits/`, squads-only. No Tier 1 touched. Hard Rule #10 means I need your explicit nod on that crossing before Step 1.

## Still blocking

Three of the ten open questions gate specific steps. Two have workable defaults you can just accept:

- **OQ-3** (size-selector hover/pressed not in Figma) → ship none, commented, per the `pageButton` precedent.
- **OQ-2** (badge) → unstyled `ReactNode` pass-through, placement only. Honest caveat: that **doesn't fully satisfy the AC**, since the AC lists a badge for PLP and Wishlist.

The third I won't decide for you.

**One process note:** I skipped `/feature-spec` and `/scope-check`. The plan's file manifest already *is* the scope, tier-classified against `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md` and CODEOWNERS directly — running scope-check on a prompt I'd write myself from that same manifest would be circular. Say the word if you'd rather I run it anyway.

Plan at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md`.

decision = """
---

## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)

> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*

The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:

**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:

- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.

Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.

**Two knock-on changes to the step pass criteria:**

1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no
   arrows**, so it becomes the only position signal — hiding it would be a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs an
   accessible position announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden "Image 3 of 8" live region, or `role="group"` with
   `aria-label`). Revised criterion: exposed and announced when it is the sole affordance.
2. **Step 4 — mobile image paging has no mechanism and no AC.** If the indicator shows position on touch, some
   touch gesture must change the image. No AC covers this; the ACs only describe desktop hover. See OQ-11.
"""

s = s.replace("### Step 4 — `ZimmProductCardMedia` molecule · *blocked on OQ-1*",

s = s.replace("- Prev/next are native `<button>` with `aria-label` via `defineMessages`, ≥ 24×24, wrapping at both ends.",

# 4. Add OQ-11
s = s.rstrip() + """
| 11 | **Mobile/tablet image paging mechanism.** §4a puts the position indicator on touch, which implies a gesture changes the image — but no AC covers mobile paging at all, and no Figma node shows a swipe affordance. | Step 4's touch branch | **none — needs an answer.** Options: native CSS scroll-snap carousel (matches the base `ProductScroller` precedent), tappable dots, or no paging at all on touch (indicator shows a static 1-of-N) |

content.text:
Recorded. Your answer resolved it cleanly, and it turned out to be capability-based rather than width-based.

**The gate is `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`** — the same one every other hover rule already uses. Hover-capable fine pointer gets arrows on hover; everything else gets the indicator, always visible. Never both. Keying it to capability rather than width is what actually delivers your intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet, and a pure width rule would hand it arrows it can never hover to reveal.

Two things fell out of that:

**The indicator can't be `aria-hidden` any more.** My original criterion had it hidden as duplicate, because the arrow buttons announced position. Where the indicator now renders there *are* no arrows — so it's the sole position signal, and hiding it is a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs a real announcement ("Image 3 of 8").

**And it surfaced a gap.** If the indicator shows position on touch, something has to change the image — but no AC covers mobile paging at all. The ACs only ever describe desktop hover.

## Where the plan stands

Complete and written to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md`. Seven steps, 21 new files, one Tier 2 touch.

Two things I need before handing to `zimmerMANNBuild`:

1. **Your nod on the Tier 2 crossing** — `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`, six append-only recipe registrations. Hard Rule #10 wants that said out loud.
2. **The question below.**

And one you should push back on now if you're going to: **the badge default knowingly under-delivers.** The AC lists a badge for PLP and Wishlist, but there's no badge node in the card set, `plp.md:71` says badges aren't in PLP designs, and TSD-SFCC-225 only delivers `c_productBadges` on the product *GET* hook — so it won't be in search-sourced tile data anyway. The plan ships an unstyled `ReactNode` pass-through with placement only. That's a slot with nothing to put in it. Tell me if you'd rather drop the badge from scope entirely and amend the AC.

answers.Putting the position indicator on touch: let's talk about this further, what is the matter at hand? ELI5

content.text:
Fair — let me lay it out plainly.

## The situation

A product has multiple photos. The Figma `Slide indicator` has variants for 5 and 8 images, so we're talking up to eight per card.

**On desktop that's fully specified.** You hover the card, arrows fade in, you click through. Done.

**On a phone, you told me the dots show instead of the arrows.** And that's right — there's no hover on a touchscreen, so arrows that only appear on hover would never appear at all.

## The gap

Dots are a **readout, not a control**. They tell you *"you're on photo 3 of 8."* They don't move you anywhere.

So on a phone, the card says "there are 8 photos, you're on the first one" — and nothing in the ACs or in any Figma node says how you get to the second one.

That's it. That's the whole problem: we're showing a progress indicator for a thing the shopper has no documented way to progress.

## Why I stopped rather than picked

Three reasons this isn't a safe default:

1. **It's most of your traffic.** Mobile-first luxury retail — this is the primary experience, not an edge case.
2. **The options aren't cosmetically different.** One is a scroll container, one turns the dots into buttons, one does nothing. Different build, different a11y story, different feel.
3. **The dots are 1px tall in Figma.** Genuinely — `159.11 × 1`. If they become tap targets they need to grow to 24×24 to be legal under WCAG 2.2, which visibly departs from what Kiera drew. That's a design change, not an implementation detail, and it's not mine to make.

## What I'd do

**Swipe, via native CSS scroll-snap.** Concretely: the images sit in a horizontally scrollable strip, the phone's normal drag gesture moves between them, and the dots follow along as a passive readout — exactly as designed, no visual change.

Four reasons it's the strong pick:

- **Your repo already does this.** The base `ProductScroller` uses `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` — same technique, already proven in this codebase.
- **It's what shoppers already expect.** Every product card on every mobile store works this way; nobody needs teaching.
- **Accessibility is free.** A scroll container is natively keyboard-scrollable and screen-reader navigable. Custom tap-dots mean building focus management by hand.
- **Zero bundle cost.** It's CSS. No gesture library, no JS listeners on 60 tiles.

The one honest caveat: swipe is invisible until you try it. There's no affordance saying "swipe me" beyond the dots implying more content exists. That's the universal convention though, and the alternative — enlarging the dots into buttons — trades an invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control.

**My recommendation: scroll-snap, and flag to Kiera that the mobile gesture was undocumented so it gets added to the spec rather than discovered in QA.**

Want me to take that, or would you rather park the touch branch and build the desktop path first? The desktop side is fully specified and completely unblocked either way.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `SFCC-236 — plan at ~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md, gate at ~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/findings.md. Gate passed, all blocking questions resolved, Tier 2 crossing (overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts) approved by Marcel. Scope is SFCC-236 only — SFCC-83/SFCC-84 stay held. Branch not yet cut; plan's Pre-flight step 1 is: git fetch origin && git checkout -b feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component origin/develop (current checkout is a merged SFCC-91 branch, do not build on it).` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```

Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

10	## 1. Goal
11	
12	Build the shared Zimmermann Product Card per SFCC-236 (8 pts, Sprint 4, epic SFCC-2), designed in Figma
13	`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` set `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size × State × Type × Unavailable), following the

68	
69	Root `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`, each with `index.tsx` · `index.stories.tsx` · `index.test.tsx` · `<name>.css.ts`:
70

73	atoms/zimmSizeSelectorOption/
74	molecules/zimmSizeSelector/

81	PLP, Search, Home, Cart, PDP and empty-search-results, and `product-list/index.jsx:51-53` imports

90	## 4. Architecture decisions
91	
92	**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
93	`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
94	`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
95	card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).
96	
97	```
98	ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
99	  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
100	              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
101	  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
102	  'home':     —
103	  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
104	```
105	
106	`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
107	`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.
108	
109	The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`
110	(`showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showRemove`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`,
111	`hoverSwapsImage`). That is what satisfies the extensibility AC: add a union member + a config row, touch no JSX.
112	
113	**The card is fluid, not 288px.** `gridSystem.ts` has `maxWidth: 'none'`. Figma's 288/179 are widths at the
114	reference artboards. The card fills its grid cell (`width: 100%`); the image holds ratio via `aspectRatio`.
115	Grid placement belongs to SFCC-80.
116	
117	**Mobile/desktop boundary = 768px** (`breakpoints.md`, 48em) — the only confirmed foundation breakpoint between
118	the 402 and 1440 artboards, and where the grid already goes 4→8 columns. `min-width` is inclusive, so the 768
119	artboard gets the desktop card. Every hover rule is additionally gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`
120	so a 768px touch tablet never gets hover-only content. See OQ-5.
121	
122	**Hover is CSS-only, keyed on `:hover, :focus-within`.** No React hover state — 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer
123	move is a PLP perf defect. `:focus-within` is not optional: WCAG 2.2 AA requires the revealed size selector and
124	arrows be keyboard-reachable. All reveal selectors live in one place, the organism's recipe root part, selecting
125	descendants by the shared `data-card-slot` constants. Molecules stay hover-agnostic.
126	
127	**One link per card (stretched-link).** The card holds a bag button, arrows, size options and a remove button —
128	nesting those in an `<a>` is invalid HTML and an a11y failure. The link wraps the product name only and carries
129	a `::after { position:absolute; inset:0 }` overlay; controls get `position:relative; z-index:1`. `href` arrives
130	pre-prefixed from the page. Uses `import {Link as RouteLink} from 'react-router-dom'` per `zimmColourSwatch` —
131	there is no `overrides/app/components/link/` override, contrary to a claim in `overrideStyling.md`.
132	
133	**Reuse, don't rebuild:** `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmIcon` (`bag`, `close`, `chevron-left`,
134	`chevron-right` all exist in `ICON_MAP`). No new icons.
135	
136	**VIC pricing is not a card concern** — precedence is the page mapper's job. Deferred to SFCC-778 (OQ-6).
137

139	
140	## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
141	
142	> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*
143	
144	The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:
145	
146	**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
147	`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:
148	
149	- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
150	- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.
151	
152	Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
153	and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
154	card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
155	a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
156	indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.
157	
158	**Two knock-on changes to the step pass criteria:**
159	
160	1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
161	   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no
162	   arrows**, so it becomes the only position signal — hiding it would be a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs an
163	   accessible position announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden "Image 3 of 8" live region, or `role="group"` with
164	   `aria-label`). Revised criterion: exposed and announced when it is the sole affordance.
165	2. **Step 4 — mobile image paging has no mechanism and no AC.** If the indicator shows position on touch, some
166	   touch gesture must change the image. No AC covers this; the ACs only describe desktop hover. See OQ-11.
167	
168	---
169	
170	## 4b. Touch image paging — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
171	
172	> *"scroll-snap it is"*
173	
174	Native CSS scroll-snap. The dots remain a **passive readout**, visually unchanged from Figma — no enlargement,
175	no conversion to tap targets, so no departure from the design and no WCAG 2.5.8 problem to solve.
176	
177	**Implementation shape: one scroll container on every breakpoint, not two mechanisms.**
178	
179	The image strip is always a horizontally scrollable flex container with `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` and
180	`scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` on each slide. What differs by pointer capability is only the *affordance* layered
181	over it:
182	
183	| | Mechanism | Affordance |
184	|---|---|---|
185	| hover + fine pointer | same scroll container | arrows call `scrollBy()`; no indicator |
186	| touch | same scroll container | native drag; indicator reflects position |
187	
188	One container rather than two code paths means a single source of truth for "which image is showing", the
189	arrows become progressive enhancement over something that already works, and the desktop path inherits
190	keyboard scrollability for free.
191	
192	**Active-index derivation:** prefer `IntersectionObserver` on the slides over a scroll listener — 60 tiles on a
193	PLP make a per-scroll-event listener a real perf cost, and the repo already has
194	`overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` (**Tier 2 — import it, do not modify it**). The `scrollend`
195	event is an acceptable alternative. Left to the Implementer; either satisfies the pass criteria.
196	
197	**Precedent:** the base `ProductScroller`
198	(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx:79-84`) already uses
199	`scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` with `overflowX: 'scroll'`. Same technique, already proven in this codebase.
200	
201	**Accepted caveat:** swipe has no explicit affordance beyond the dots implying further content. This is the
202	universal mobile convention, and the alternative (enlarging 1px dots into 24×24 tap targets) trades an
203	invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control. **Action: flag to Kiera that the mobile
204	gesture is undocumented in the design**, so it lands in the spec rather than being discovered in QA.
205	
206	**Added Step 4 pass criteria:**
207	- The slide container carries `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`; every slide carries `scrollSnapAlign`.
208	- Arrows are rendered only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; the indicator only outside it; assert the
209	  two never coexist in the same DOM.
210	- Arrow activation moves the scroll position (assert `scrollBy`/`scrollTo` is called — jsdom does not lay out,
211	  so assert the call, not the resulting offset).
212	- The indicator's active index tracks the observed slide, and clamps at both ends.
213	- A single-image product renders no indicator, no arrows, and no horizontal overflow.
214	- No gesture library is added — `package.json` is untouched (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7).

264	- **🟡 The badge looks interactive, against a requirement that says it must not be.** `Tag` wraps its label in

274	  (30×8), not an instance of `40001471:20752` (33×15). The design system has a Badge component the card

279	- `Tag` renders top-left when `badge` is supplied; absent from the DOM when not. **Non-interactive** — not a

298	## 6. Steps

# SFCC-236 — Product Card Shared Component: Build Plan

**Generated:** 2026-09-02 · **Planner:** `zm-planner` (Opus) · **Gate:** [findings.md](./findings.md)
**STATUS: GATE PASSED — ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`.** All blocking questions resolved; Tier 2 crossing approved
by Marcel 2026-09-02. Branch not yet cut (skill rule: never create a branch unasked).
**Scope: SFCC-236 only.** SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 are held — blocked on data source, surface list, and Legal's consent ruling.

---

## 1. Goal

Build the shared Zimmermann Product Card per SFCC-236 (8 pts, Sprint 4, epic SFCC-2), designed in Figma
`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` set `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size × State × Type × Unavailable), following the
FED handbook's ui-kits atomic layering and the PR #64 / `zimmColourSwatchGroup` pattern — named-export
component reading a `Zimm*`-namespaced multipart recipe via `useMultiStyleConfig`, parts applied with
`<chakra.div __css={styles.x}>`, all values `var(--zimm-*)` with explicit media queries.

**The card is the visual layer only:** every value arrives as a prop, it owns no data fetching, and it renders
the add-to-bag / size-selection controls without wiring their behaviour (SFCC-185 / SFCC-497 / SFCC-90).

---

## 2. Scale call — one branch, seven commits, one PR

```bash
git fetch origin && git checkout -b feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component origin/develop
```

The current checkout (`feature/SFCC-91_...`) is merged and must not be built on.

**Why one branch despite ~24 files:** one component family, one Figma set, one ticket, one reviewer set
(`pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` on every file). The molecules have exactly one consumer — the organism — so
merging them separately merges dead code. Splitting would also multiply the single Tier 2 touch
(`theme/components/index.ts`) across three approval cycles for an append-only registry edit.

**Full build loop (Implementer → Tester → Scorer per step).** This is a keystone blocking eight tickets, so a
wrong prop contract propagates into eight downstream stories.

### Deliberately dropped

| Dropped | Why |
|---|---|
| Copy-first | Nothing to copy — no file is being overridden at a mirrored path |
| Playwright / `.feature` | No page renders this component on this branch; E2E belongs to SFCC-80/90/497 |
| Bundle-size / LCP step | Nothing imports the card yet; bundle delta is zero |
| Visual regression | Chromatic/Loki is out of budget (`testing.md` excludes it); hover fidelity is a manual Storybook check |
| Multi-region fixtures | The card takes pre-formatted strings; no locale/currency logic to vary |

**Retained, non-negotiable:** `npx tsc --noEmit` · `npm run test` · `npm run lint` · `npm run audit:tokens` ·
`cr review --light --base develop`.

---

## 3. File manifest

### Modified (3)

| File | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | **Tier 2** | `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` (CODEOWNERS:117) |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx` | 3/4 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.test.tsx` | 3/4 | same |

**The Tier 2 file is the only tier crossing.** AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 → needs explicit scope confirmation
before Step 1. No Tier 1 file is touched.

### Created (21) — all Tier 3/4, `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b`

Root `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`, each with `index.tsx` · `index.stories.tsx` · `index.test.tsx` · `<name>.css.ts`:

```
molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/
atoms/zimmSizeSelectorOption/
molecules/zimmSizeSelector/
molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/
molecules/zimmProductCardContent/
organisms/zimmProductCard/          + zimmProductCardShared.ts
```

**Explicitly NOT created: `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`** — creating it activates the resolver for
PLP, Search, Home, Cart, PDP and empty-search-results, and `product-list/index.jsx:51-53` imports
`{Skeleton as ProductTileSkeleton}`, so an override without that named export breaks PLP at import time.

`zimmProductCardShared.ts` holds DOM-contract constants (`data-card-slot` names) + `CARD_BP` derived from
`theme/foundation/gridSystem`. No design values, so it stays co-located (precedent:
`zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`). Keeps the Tier 2 surface at exactly one file.

---

## 4. Architecture decisions

**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).

```
ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
  'home':     —
  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
```

`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.

The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`
(`showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showRemove`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`,
`hoverSwapsImage`). That is what satisfies the extensibility AC: add a union member + a config row, touch no JSX.

**The card is fluid, not 288px.** `gridSystem.ts` has `maxWidth: 'none'`. Figma's 288/179 are widths at the
reference artboards. The card fills its grid cell (`width: 100%`); the image holds ratio via `aspectRatio`.
Grid placement belongs to SFCC-80.

**Mobile/desktop boundary = 768px** (`breakpoints.md`, 48em) — the only confirmed foundation breakpoint between
the 402 and 1440 artboards, and where the grid already goes 4→8 columns. `min-width` is inclusive, so the 768
artboard gets the desktop card. Every hover rule is additionally gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`
so a 768px touch tablet never gets hover-only content. See OQ-5.

**Hover is CSS-only, keyed on `:hover, :focus-within`.** No React hover state — 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer
move is a PLP perf defect. `:focus-within` is not optional: WCAG 2.2 AA requires the revealed size selector and
arrows be keyboard-reachable. All reveal selectors live in one place, the organism's recipe root part, selecting
descendants by the shared `data-card-slot` constants. Molecules stay hover-agnostic.

**One link per card (stretched-link).** The card holds a bag button, arrows, size options and a remove button —
nesting those in an `<a>` is invalid HTML and an a11y failure. The link wraps the product name only and carries
a `::after { position:absolute; inset:0 }` overlay; controls get `position:relative; z-index:1`. `href` arrives
pre-prefixed from the page. Uses `import {Link as RouteLink} from 'react-router-dom'` per `zimmColourSwatch` —
there is no `overrides/app/components/link/` override, contrary to a claim in `overrideStyling.md`.

**Reuse, don't rebuild:** `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmIcon` (`bag`, `close`, `chevron-left`,
`chevron-right` all exist in `ICON_MAP`). No new icons.

**VIC pricing is not a card concern** — precedence is the page mapper's job. Deferred to SFCC-778 (OQ-6).

---

## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)

> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*

The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:

**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:

- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.

Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.

**Two knock-on changes to the step pass criteria:**

1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no
   arrows**, so it becomes the only position signal — hiding it would be a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs an
   accessible position announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden "Image 3 of 8" live region, or `role="group"` with
   `aria-label`). Revised criterion: exposed and announced when it is the sole affordance.
2. **Step 4 — mobile image paging has no mechanism and no AC.** If the indicator shows position on touch, some
   touch gesture must change the image. No AC covers this; the ACs only describe desktop hover. See OQ-11.

---

## 4b. Touch image paging — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)

> *"scroll-snap it is"*

Native CSS scroll-snap. The dots remain a **passive readout**, visually unchanged from Figma — no enlargement,
no conversion to tap targets, so no departure from the design and no WCAG 2.5.8 problem to solve.

**Implementation shape: one scroll container on every breakpoint, not two mechanisms.**

The image strip is always a horizontally scrollable flex container with `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` and
`scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` on each slide. What differs by pointer capability is only the *affordance* layered
over it:

| | Mechanism | Affordance |
|---|---|---|
| hover + fine pointer | same scroll container | arrows call `scrollBy()`; no indicator |
| touch | same scroll container | native drag; indicator reflects position |

One container rather than two code paths means a single source of truth for "which image is showing", the
arrows become progressive enhancement over something that already works, and the desktop path inherits
keyboard scrollability for free.

**Active-index derivation:** prefer `IntersectionObserver` on the slides over a scroll listener — 60 tiles on a
PLP make a per-scroll-event listener a real perf cost, and the repo already has
`overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` (**Tier 2 — import it, do not modify it**). The `scrollend`
event is an acceptable alternative. Left to the Implementer; either satisfies the pass criteria.

**Precedent:** the base `ProductScroller`
(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx:79-84`) already uses
`scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` with `overflowX: 'scroll'`. Same technique, already proven in this codebase.

**Accepted caveat:** swipe has no explicit affordance beyond the dots implying further content. This is the
universal mobile convention, and the alternative (enlarging 1px dots into 24×24 tap targets) trades an
invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control. **Action: flag to Kiera that the mobile
gesture is undocumented in the design**, so it lands in the spec rather than being discovered in QA.

**Added Step 4 pass criteria:**
- The slide container carries `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`; every slide carries `scrollSnapAlign`.
- Arrows are rendered only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; the indicator only outside it; assert the
  two never coexist in the same DOM.
- Arrow activation moves the scroll position (assert `scrollBy`/`scrollTo` is called — jsdom does not lay out,
  so assert the call, not the resulting offset).
- The indicator's active index tracks the observed slide, and clamps at both ends.
- A single-image product renders no indicator, no arrows, and no horizontal overflow.
- No gesture library is added — `package.json` is untouched (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7).

---

## 4c. Badge — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02), and it corrects the decomposition

Nine nodes supplied; all resolve off one parent, `40001471:20702` "Badge" (a documentation board).
`40001471:20682` is its cover slide, not a component.

**There are TWO badge components, not one:**

| Component set | Node | Variants | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`Badge`** | `40001471:20752` | `State=Primary` (`…20751`) · `State=Hover` (`…20750`) | 33×15 |
| **`Stock Status Badge`** | `40001796:7041` | `State=Available` (`…7040`) · `State=Unavailable` (`…7039`) · `State=Low stock` (`…7038`) | 66–79×20 |

`Stock Status Badge` appears in **no acceptance criterion**. It maps to `.docs/prd/plp.md` §3
("**OUT OF STOCK** shown on tile when all sizes are at or below buffer threshold" and the low-stock
indicator) — so the PRD requirement that had no design **does** have one. Its `Low stock` state
corresponds to nothing in any AC, and `plp.md` §3 places low-stock *at size level*, not on the tile.

### Decomposition correction — three slots move from Content to Media

Reading `Image Group / Size=Large` (`40002742:46322`, 288×432) and `Size=Small` (`40002742:46321`,
179×268) shows the overlays live on the **image**, not in the text block:

| Slot | Frame | Structure | Desktop | Mobile |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| **`Close`** (remove 'x') | 48×48 @ top-right | `touchContainer` 24×24 → `Icon` 16×16 | ✅ | ✅ |
| **`Carousel`** (arrows) | 288×24 @ y=204 (vertically centred) | two `touchContainer` 24×24 @ x=12 and x=252 | ✅ | **absent** |
| **`Slide-indicator`** | 179×1, flush to the image's bottom edge (y=267 of 268) | instance | **absent** | ✅ |

1. **The badge slot moves from Step 5 to Step 4.** It is `Tag`, overlaid top-left on the image — not a part
   of `Card-content`. Remove the `badge` part from `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`; add a `tag` part to
   `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`.
2. **The remove ('x') CTA moves from Step 5 to Step 4.** It is `Close`, top-right on the image. The plan had
   it in `ZimmProductCardContent` — wrong molecule. Remove `onRemove` handling from Content; it belongs in
   Media. The union still carries `onRemove` on the wishlist member; the organism passes it to Media.
3. **This makes the split cleaner, not messier:** everything overlaid on the image is Media, everything below
   it is Content.
4. **§4a and §4b are confirmed by the design itself,** not just by the verbal decision — `Size=Large` has
   `Carousel` and no indicator; `Size=Small` has `Slide-indicator` and no `Carousel`.
5. **The slide indicator is a 1px hairline flush to the image's bottom edge**, not floating dots. Step 1's
   recipe must not assume dot geometry.

### Two new findings that need raising, not resolving in code

- **🟡 The badge looks interactive, against a requirement that says it must not be.** `Tag` wraps its label in
  a **`touchContainer`** — this file's convention for an interactive hit area (the bag icon and both arrows use
  the identical wrapper) — and the `Badge` component ships a **`State=Hover`**. But SPR-16 reads
  "~~clickable~~ product badges" and `.docs/prd/plp.md:70` says clickable badges are *"a NEW unsigned request —
  not confirmed… **Do not implement**."* Two independent signals in Figma versus an explicit written
  prohibition. **Build it non-interactive per the requirement** (a plain element, no button, no hover rule),
  and raise the discrepancy — do not resolve it in code.
- **🔵 `Icons OLD`.** The `Carousel` arrows in the current card design instance icons named
  `Icons OLD` (`40003066:50796`, `40003066:50798`). Deprecated naming inside a live component. Flag to Kiera.
- **🔵 The card's `Tag` does not instance the `Badge` component.** `Tag`'s child is a raw `Label` text node
  (30×8), not an instance of `40001471:20752` (33×15). The design system has a Badge component the card
  doesn't use. Ask which is authoritative before styling the slot.

### Revised Step 4 pass criteria (additions)

- `Tag` renders top-left when `badge` is supplied; absent from the DOM when not. **Non-interactive** — not a
  `<button>`, no `_hover` rule, no `tabIndex`. A comment cites SPR-16 / `plp.md:70` for why.
- `Close` renders top-right **only** for the wishlist variation, is a native `<button>` with an `aria-label`
  naming the product, hit area ≥ 24×24, and calls `onRemove`.
- Stock status is **out of scope for SFCC-236** unless the developer says otherwise — it is unmentioned in
  every AC, and its `Low stock` state contradicts `plp.md` §3's size-level placement. See OQ-12.

## 6. Steps

One commit each, conventional subject with `(SFCC-236)` suffix (enforced by `scripts/hooks/commit-msg`).

### Step 1 — `ZimmSlideIndicator` molecule · *touch-only, see §4a*
Figma `40002536:7957`. Display-only dot/bar strip. Props `count`, `activeIndex`. Recipe parts `['root','dot']`,
`baseStyle` a function of `{isActive}`. Story `Elements/ZimmSlideIndicator`.

- Renders exactly `count` nodes; exactly one active for any `activeIndex` in range.
- Out-of-range clamps rather than throwing; `count <= 1` renders nothing.
- **Exposed and announced, NOT `aria-hidden`** (revised per §4a) — where it renders there are no arrows, so it is the sole position signal.
- `parts` exactly equals the `styles.*` reads. Registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

### Step 2 — `ZimmSizeSelectorOption` atom + `ZimmSizeSelector` molecule · *blocked on OQ-3*
Mirrors the `zimmColourSwatch` / `zimmColourSwatchGroup` pair. Figma `40003038:125876` and `40003066:34868`.
Option renders native `<button role="radio" aria-checked>`. Group is `role="radiogroup"` with roving tabindex
and arrow-key nav copied from `zimmColourSwatchGroup`'s `handleSwatchesKeyDown`. "One Size" renders a single
non-interactive label, not a radio group.

- **Default / Selected / Focus / Disabled** all present and distinguishable, matching the four Figma states.
  Focus uses `outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)'` + `outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)'`.
  Disabled sets the native attribute (genuinely inert for AT).
- **Hover and Active are not in the Figma set — do not invent them.** Ship with no `_hover`/`_active` and a
  comment saying so (`pageButton` precedent). This is OQ-3.
- Arrow keys cycle and wrap, skip disabled; Tab enters the group once and leaves it once.
- Every hit area ≥ 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8).
- `onSelect` fires with `value` on click and arrow nav; never for a disabled option.
- Tests wrap in `IntlProvider` + `MemoryRouter`, mock `useMultiStyleConfig` flat, mock the icons barrel.

### Step 3 — `ZimmProductPrice`: add opt-out `isLive` prop
`ZimmProductPrice` hardcodes `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` — correct on PDP (SC 4.1.3) but wrong
replicated 60× across a PLP grid where no price changes after mount. Add `isLive?: boolean` defaulting `true`.

**Independently droppable** — nothing downstream depends on it; drop the commit if the reviewer disagrees.

- Default renders both attributes exactly as today. `isLive={false}` renders neither, in both the loaded and
  `isLoading` branches.
- Existing test + story pass unmodified except the two added cases. Diff is additive only.

### Step 4 — `ZimmProductCardMedia` molecule · *see §4a and §4b*
Figma `40002742:46323` / `40000301:4718`. Props `primaryImage`, `hoverImage?`, `images?`, `swapOnHover`,
`showControls`. Holds the paging index in local `useState`. Stamps `data-card-slot` attributes so the organism's
recipe can reveal them.

- **AC1 — primary image renders in every configuration**, including with `hoverImage`/`images`/`showControls`
  all absent. Assert across all six variation × unavailable combinations.
- Every `<img>` has a non-empty `alt` (or explicit `alt=""` with rationale) — enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`.
- `loading="lazy"` + `decoding="async"` on non-primary; primary accepts a `priority` escape hatch (LCP ≤ 2s p75
  mobile; PLP tiles are LCP candidates).
- Aspect ratio from the recipe, root `width: 100%`. Assert no `288px`/`179px` literal anywhere.
- Prev/next are native `<button>` with `aria-label` via `defineMessages`, ≥ 24×24, wrapping at both ends — rendered **only** under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; the indicator renders only outside it. Assert the two never coexist.
- Single-image product renders no controls and no indicator.
- Hover swap is done by the recipe, not JS: both images in DOM, opacity/visibility keyed off the shared selector.
- No data fetching, no SDK hooks; `useIntl` only.

### Step 5 — `ZimmProductCardContent` molecule
Figma `40002109:26908` (Desktop `26906` / Mobile `37103`), verified structure:
`Content(40,32,208x138) > Frame(208x82) > [Product name and attributes(208x49) > [name+icons(208x25),
Attributes(0,41,208x8)], Price(0,73), Size Selector(0,106, hidden), Link(0,114,57x24)]`.

Takes booleans derived from `VARIATION_CONFIG`, never a `variation` literal — so it never knows the variation names.
Recipe parts: `['root','nameRow','nameLink','icons','bagButton','attributes','price','sizeSlot','notifyMe','message']` (no `badge` — see §4c).

  `ZimmIcon type="bag"` `aria-hidden`. **Bag, per the verified `Icon_bag` — not a wishlist star.** Hover/active:
  no Figma spec → no rule, commented. Focus: standard ring. Disabled when `isUnavailable`, native `disabled`,
  and `onAddToBag` must not fire.
- ~~Remove ('x')~~ **moved to Step 4 (§4c)** — it is the `Close` overlay on the image, not a Card-content part.
- Attributes row renders `colour`+`size` for wishlist, **absent from the DOM** (not hidden) for plp/home.

  hover reveal/hide is pure CSS.
- Notify-me renders only when `isUnavailable` **and** `onNotifyMe` supplied. Copy via `defineMessages`, id in
  the `product_view.*` namespace per the `zimmProductPrice` precedent.
- Exactly one heading per card, at the caller's `headingLevel`.
- ~~Badge~~ **moved to Step 4 (§4c)** — it is the `Tag` overlay on the image, not a Card-content part.
- Responsive via explicit `@media (min-width: ${CARD_BP.desktop})` off the shared module — never array shorthand.

### Step 6 — `ZimmProductCard` organism + variation config + shared module
Creates `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, the union, `VARIATION_CONFIG`, the composition, the stretched link, and
`zimmProductCard.css.ts` holding **all** hover-reveal rules.

- Union enforced at compile time: `variation:'wishlist'` without `onRemove`/`colour`/`size` fails `tsc`;
  `variation:'home'` given `onRemove` fails `tsc`. Two `@ts-expect-error` cases — these are the extensibility
  AC's real proof.

  from the config object.
- **AC1 across all variations:** six cases (plp/home/wishlist × unavailable true/false) assert the primary image.
- **Exactly one `<a>` per card** — `getAllByRole('link')` length 1. Every control separately focusable.
- Keyboard equivalence: with `:focus-within`, size options and arrows are Tab-reachable in jsdom.

  `:hover, :focus-within` key, (b) nested inside `@media (min-width: ...) and (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`,
  (c) the selector targets the imported `data-card-slot` constants, not a string literal.

- Recipe key is `ZimmProductCard`, not `ProductCard` (`recipeGuards.test.ts:357`).
- All six recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
- Story `Commerce/ZimmProductCard`: `Default` (mandatory), `PLP`, `PLPOutOfStock`, `Home`, `Wishlist`,

  hover-dependent story carries a docs note for manual review.

- `ZimmProductCardProps` and the three member types **are exported** (deviating from the exemplar) because they
  are the contract SFCC-80/90/497 will type their mappers against. Document the deviation in JSDoc.

`tsc --noEmit` · `lint` · `test` · `audit:tokens` · `coderabbit auth status` then `cr review --light --base develop`.

Build Step 1 of the SFCC-236 plan ONLY — full plan at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md, but here is everything you need for this step.

## Step 1 — `ZimmSlideIndicator` molecule

Create ONLY these 4 files:
```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/index.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/index.stories.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/index.test.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts
```
Plus register it in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (add one import + one entry to the existing `components` export object — do not touch any other line in that file).

**Do not touch any other file. Do not create any other component from the plan (that's later steps).**

## Design source
Figma `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`, node `40002536:7957` "Slide indicator" — a 1px-tall hairline strip (verified: 159.11×1 / 99.44×1 depending on `Qty images`), flush to the image's bottom edge. NOT floating dots — do not assume dot geometry; render it as a segmented hairline/bar strip matching that 1px height, one segment per image, the active segment visually distinguished (e.g. differing opacity/width via the recipe). 13 Figma variants total: `Qty images` = 5 | 8, `Slide selected` = 1..N.

## CRITICAL — this is NOT a duplicate-with-arrows situation, it is touch-ONLY
Per the plan's §4a (Marcel's resolved decision): "position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows." This component is the read-only position indicator that appears ONLY where hover is unavailable (touch devices). It has NO buttons, NO click handlers — it is purely a visual + accessible readout of "which image am I on". The arrows (a separate component, built in a later step) are what desktop uses instead.

## Reference pattern to copy exactly
Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` and its sibling `.css.ts`, `.stories.tsx`, `.test.tsx` FIRST, in full, before writing anything. Copy its conventions precisely:
- Named export (PascalCase, e.g. `export const ZimmSlideIndicator = (...) => {...}`) AND a default export (`export default ZimmSlideIndicator`) — this component has no lazy-load consumer yet but match the existing dual-export convention used across ui-kits atoms/molecules for consistency.
- Props type declared inline at top of file, named `ZimmSlideIndicatorProps`, NOT exported (no sibling needs it — this component's props are primitive: `count: number`, `activeIndex: number`).
- Recipe key as a module-level string const: `const ZIMM_SLIDE_INDICATOR_RECIPE = 'ZimmSlideIndicator'`.
- `useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_SLIDE_INDICATOR_RECIPE, {isActive})` — actually the props object passed should be whatever the per-segment styling needs; study exactly how zimmColourSwatchGroup passes its props object to the recipe and match that shape (it may be at the root call, with `isActive` applied per rendered element — read the exemplar closely, don't guess).
- Apply parts via `<chakra.div __css={styles.partName}>` — `__css`, not `sx`, `chakra.*` primitives not `Box`/`Flex`.
- All colour/spacing values in the `.css.ts` file as `var(--zimm-*)` custom properties. NEVER a bare Chakra token key (e.g. `gap: 'xs'` is FORBIDDEN — must be `gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`). This is mechanically enforced by `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` — your test run will fail if you get this wrong.
- Responsive values (if any) as explicit `[`@media (min-width: ${BP.x})`]` blocks — never Chakra's array shorthand `['a','b','c']`, which the same guard test fails on every element.

## Recipe file (`zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts`)
```ts
export const ZimmSlideIndicator = {
  parts: ['root', 'dot'],
  baseStyle: (props: {isActive?: boolean}): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({ ... }),
};
```
No default export. The recipe key name `ZimmSlideIndicator` must NOT collide with any base SFCC recipe name — it doesn't, this is a net-new name, so you're safe, but confirm by checking `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/components/` has no `slide-indicator.js` or similar (there is a guard test in `recipeGuards.test.ts` for this — read it to understand what it checks).

## Registration
In `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`, add:
```ts
import {ZimmSlideIndicator} from '../../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/zimmSlideIndicator.css'
```
(match the exact relative-path style already used for the other ui-kits imports in that file — read the file first to copy the exact import path convention), and add `ZimmSlideIndicator,` to the `components` export object, matching alphabetical/grouping convention already present.

## Component behaviour and exact pass criteria (all must be true)
- Props: `count: number`, `activeIndex: number`.
- Renders exactly `count` segment/dot nodes as children of the `root` part.
- Exactly one node carries the "active" treatment, for any `activeIndex` value that is `>= 0` and `< count`.
- **Out-of-range `activeIndex` clamps rather than throwing** — if `activeIndex < 0`, treat as `0`; if `activeIndex >= count`, treat as `count - 1`. Write this clamping explicitly, do not rely on `Array.map` silently doing nothing sensible.
- **`count <= 1` renders nothing** — return `null` (or render the root with zero children — but the test should assert nothing meaningful is on screen; prefer returning `null` from the component entirely for `count <= 0`, and also for `count === 1` since a single image has nothing to indicate position among).
- **The root is EXPOSED and ANNOUNCED to assistive tech — it must NOT be `aria-hidden`.** This is a corrected requirement (see §4a of the plan): because this indicator is the ONLY position signal on touch devices (no arrows exist there to announce it instead), hiding it would be a WCAG 1.1.1 information-loss violation. Implement an accessible announcement of position — e.g. a visually-hidden text node inside the root reading something like "Image {activeIndex + 1} of {count}" (use `defineMessages` + `useIntl` with a parameterized message, matching the i18n convention in `zimmColourSwatchGroup`), OR `role="group"` with a computed `aria-label` of the same shape. Pick whichever matches the exemplar's i18n conventions most closely. Do NOT ship it aria-hidden — a test will explicitly assert this.
- `parts` array in the recipe must EXACTLY equal the set of `styles.X` reads in `index.tsx` — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` enforces this by walking your file; if you read `styles.root` and `styles.dot`, your `parts` array must be exactly `['root', 'dot']`, no more, no less.
- Component appears correctly in the `components` export in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

## Story (`index.stories.tsx`)
- `title: 'Elements/ZimmSlideIndicator'` (per `.claude/rules/components.md` categorisation — this is a generic building block, not commerce-specific by itself).
- Mandatory `Default` export.
- Named exports for meaningful states: e.g. `FiveImages` (count=5), `EightImages` (count=8), `LastSelected` (activeIndex = count-1), `FirstSelected` (activeIndex=0).
- No `play` function needed — this is a purely visual/display component with no interaction to assert (it has no click handlers).

## Test (`index.test.tsx`)
Vitest + React Testing Library. Cover, at minimum:
- Renders exactly `count` segment nodes for count=5 and count=8.
- Exactly one active segment for activeIndex at first (0), middle, and last (count-1) positions.
- `activeIndex = -1` clamps to treating index 0 as active (does not throw).
- `activeIndex = count` (i.e. one past the end) clamps to treating the last index active (does not throw).
- `count = 0` renders null / nothing.
- `count = 1` renders null / nothing.
- The root is NOT `aria-hidden="true"` — assert this explicitly (query for the root and assert `aria-hidden` attribute is absent or `false`).
- Some accessible text/label exists reflecting position (assert on whatever your accessible-announcement mechanism produces — a get-by-text match on the visually-hidden text, or an aria-label match).
- Mock `useMultiStyleConfig` to return a flat parts object (`{root: {}, dot: {}}`) so no real Chakra theme is needed — copy this mock pattern exactly from `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx`.
- Wrap renders in `IntlProvider` if you used `defineMessages`/`useIntl` (required — `useIntl` throws without a provider). Copy the render-helper pattern from the exemplar test file.

## House rules (apply to every file you write)
- TypeScript only (`.tsx`/`.ts`), no `.js`/`.jsx`.
- No `any` without a comment explaining why. No non-null assertion (`!`) without a comment.
- Australian spelling in any new identifiers/comments you author (not relevant here, no colour-adjacent naming in this component, but keep in mind for later steps).
- No hardcoded hex/px/rem/em literal anywhere in `index.tsx` or the recipe — everything through `var(--zimm-*)`.
- Do NOT add a `console.log` anywhere.
- Do not modify `package.json` — no new dependencies.

## When done
Report back: the exact list of files created/modified with line counts, and confirm you did NOT touch any file outside this list. Do NOT stage or commit anything — that happens later in the loop, after testing and scoring.

content.text:
# Visual checkpoint — Step 1, `ZimmSlideIndicator`

This step changes rendered output, so per the build loop the loop stops here for your check before it becomes a commit. All gates are green (PASS at Scorer round 2), and I've confirmed via the DOM (not just a screenshot) that it renders correctly: `role="group"`, `aria-label="Image 1 of 5"`, height exactly `1px`, width fluid (948px in the canvas, tracks the container — not a fixed 288/179px), 5 segments, first one active at `rgb(25,25,25)` (the corrected `--zimm-color-bg-05` token) and the rest at 40% opacity. No console errors.

**Please open:** `http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/commerce-zimmslideindicator--default`

It's a Storybook dev server already running on your machine — I didn't start a new one, I confirmed the existing one on :6006 is serving this branch fresh (it already reflects the post-rework `Commerce/` category).

**What to compare against, per story:**

| Story | Figma node | Compare |
|---|---|---|
| `Default` / `First Selected` | `40002536:7947` (`Qty images=5, Slide selected=1`) | 5-segment strip, first active |
| `Five Images` | `40002536:7947` | same |
| `Eight Images` | `40002536:7956` (`Qty images=8, Slide selected=1`) | 8-segment strip |
| `Last Selected` | `40002536:7950` (`Qty images=5, Slide selected=5`) | 5-segment strip, last active |

**What should be on screen:** a very thin (1px-tall) horizontal strip of segments, one per image, sitting flush wherever it's placed — this build renders it in isolation, with no image behind it yet (that's Step 4). It will look almost invisible against a white background at 100% zoom — that's correct, not a bug; the Figma node itself is a 1px hairline, not floating dots.

**What would indicate a real defect:** any segment taller than a hairline; visible gaps between segments (spec is flush-adjacent, `gap: 0`); more than one segment looking "active"; or the strip having a fixed width instead of stretching to fill whatever container it's in.

**Two things flagged as open, not defects — your call, not mine:** the exact colour pairing (active vs. 40%-opacity) and the inter-segment styling are both marked in the code as provisional pending your sign-off, since the Figma export didn't confirm them beyond the 1px height. If what's on screen looks wrong to you, it's most likely one of these two.

I'll wait for your go before this becomes a commit and I move to Step 2.

content.text:
Found a real, confirmed defect — not a colour nuance, a structural mismatch. Pulled the actual Figma renders and diffed them against the live computed styles.

**Figma ground truth** (each state fetched individually, 28×28):
- **Default**: plain text "x", **no border, no box at all**
- **Selected**: "X" inside a **bordered outline box** (not filled) — normal black text
- **Disabled**: faint grey "x", **no border, no box**
- **Focus**: bordered box **plus** an outer focus ring (34×34)

**What's actually rendering** (pulled via computed styles from the live `With Disabled Size` story, not just a screenshot):

```json
XS (default):  border: 1px solid rgb(112,112,112)   background: transparent
S  (disabled): border: 1px solid rgb(209,209,209)   background: transparent
M  (selected): border: 1px solid rgb(25,25,25)      background: rgb(25,25,25)  color: white
L  (default):  border: 1px solid rgb(112,112,112)   background: transparent
```

Every chip has a border box — Figma gives unselected and disabled chips **no box at all**, plain text only. And Selected is rendering as a solid black fill with inverted white text, where Figma shows an **outline-only** box with normal text colour.

So the actual defect is backwards from what the recipe currently expresses: **default/disabled should be borderless**, and **selected should be bordered-but-unfilled**, not filled solid.

This isn't a Figma-ambiguity situation like the earlier colour-token questions — the shape difference (box vs. no box, filled vs. outlined) is directly visible in the exported PNGs, unambiguous. I'm not committing this step. Sending it back for a rework round to match the design before either of us does a final pass.

| `resolveBorderColour` | disabled | `var(--zimm-color-border-secondary)` | `transparent` |
