## Orchestrator verdict: UNDER-scope
Everything else (badge, remove overlay, scroll-snap, ZimmSlideIndicator composition, AC1, alt text, loading, aspect ratio, wrap, single-image suppression, data-card-slot contract) fully delivered with concrete evidence. One specific gap: plan §4b says "assert the two never coexist in the same DOM" for arrows-vs-indicator — no test (DOM-based or structural-on-the-recipe) proves this, and the component's OWN test ("stamps every data-card-slot value when all optional slots are active") asserts BOTH `[data-card-slot="carousel"]` AND `[data-card-slot="indicator"]` are in the document simultaneously — the architecture is "both always in DOM, toggled by CSS `display` under a media query" (correctly avoids the opacity/visibility a11y anti-pattern per the Tester), consistent with how Step 6's plan spec ITSELF prescribes verifying equivalent hover-reveal claims later ("import the recipe object and assert... nested inside @media... gated") — but no such structural assertion exists here, and the DOM-presence claim as literally worded in the Step 4 criteria is not met. The Orchestrator judges the plan's own wording ("never coexist in the same DOM") was probably loose/pre-dated Step 6's more precise methodology, not that the architecture itself is wrong.

## Tester verdict: multiple CONFIRMED defects via real mutation testing

1. **🔴 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — same underlying issue as the Orchestrator's finding: mutation-proved zero regression coverage on the mutual-exclusivity mechanism. Deleted the entire `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` media-query gate from the recipe (arrows permanently visible regardless of pointer capability) — component's own 21 tests, recipeParts, recipeGuards, tsc, eslint, audit:tokens ALL still passed. This is because `index.test.tsx` mocks `useMultiStyleConfig` to `{}` for every part, so the real CSS is never exercised by any test.

2. **🔴 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — `close` and `arrowButton` recipe parts have ZERO `_focusVisible`/`_hover` styling. Both are real native `<button>` overlays sitting on top of photographic images with only the bare browser-default outline on keyboard focus. This breaks an established, 3-times-independently-verified codebase convention: `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`'s `pageButton`, `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`, and `zimmNavItem.css.ts` all apply the identical `outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)'` + `outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)'` pair via `_focusVisible`. No Figma citation exists either way on hover states specifically (unlike Step 2's SizeChip, where Figma explicitly enumerated 4 states with no hover/active) — this finding is about the UNIVERSAL focus-ring convention, not an invented hover treatment.

3. **🔴 CONFIRMED via fixture, ONE-OFF but real bug** — `currentIndex` state is never re-clamped when the `images` prop shrinks after the component is already mounted and navigated (e.g., a colour-variant swap that changes gallery length while the card stays on screen). Reproduced: navigate to last image of a 3-image gallery, re-render with a 2-image gallery, click "Next" — first click is a silent no-op (the internal `currentIndex` stays at the stale value 2), second click finally wraps correctly. `ZimmSlideIndicator`'s own display-side clamp masks this visually right after the shrink (shows "2 of 2", looks fine) but the component's OWN navigation math uses the stale unclamped value. Established precedent to copy exists in this exact codebase: `zimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own `useEffect` (cited in its own comments) clamps to the highest valid page when the offered set shrinks. This component's author clearly knows that precedent (referenced elsewhere in comments) but didn't apply it to `currentIndex`.

4. **🟡 CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF** — the `scrollend` listener (`index.tsx:149-161`, real non-trivial clamping logic) has ZERO test coverage. Confirmed testable under jsdom (`container.dispatchEvent(new Event('scrollend'))` works; `scrollLeft`/`clientWidth` are definable properties even without real layout) — it just wasn't written.

5. **🟡 PLAUSIBLE, reasoned from confirmed code facts, not device-tested — a real WCAG 2.1.1 gap, distinct from finding #1/#2** — `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` is a proxy for POINTER capability, not KEYBOARD presence. A device resolving this query false (touchscreen + physical keyboard, switch-access, or any `hover:none` desktop browser) gets: arrows `display:none` (unreachable), a non-interactive indicator (zero focusable content, confirmed by reading ZimmSlideIndicator's own source), and a scroll container with NO `tabIndex` and NO `onKeyDown` at all. There is currently no keyboard-operable way to page a multi-image gallery in that pointer profile — full stop. This is the single most novel and important finding: the mutual-exclusivity design conflates "show arrows vs. show indicator" with "keyboard operability vs. not," when it should be "visual affordance differs by pointer capability, but keyboard operability exists regardless."

## Your job

Score all six axes. This step has enough real, confirmed findings that a straight PASS seems unlikely — but weigh carefully what's authorized for THIS round vs. deferred:

- Finding #1/Orchestrator's UNDER verdict: same root cause. Fixable in-file by adding ONE structural test (import the real, unmocked recipe object; assert `carousel.display`/`indicatorWrapper.display` resolve to mutually-exclusive values under the media-query key) — this is exactly the technique the plan prescribes for Step 6's equivalent claim. Should this round also require reinterpreting/updating the plan's own Step 4 wording ("never coexist in the same DOM" → "never simultaneously visible/interactive, verified structurally") so it stops contradicting the architecture the rest of the build already commits to? That's a plan-doc edit, separate from a code fix — is it in your authority to direct, or should it be flagged for the orchestrating session to handle?
- Finding #2: cheap, safe, uses an existing universal token pair, zero design-invention risk (this is a mechanical a11y convention, not a Figma-sourced visual decision). Authorize as a fix.
- Finding #3: real, reproducible, has a precedent in-repo to copy. Authorize as a fix — but scope it tightly (add the clamp effect, don't restructure anything else).
- Finding #4: authorize adding test coverage for the scrollend listener, OR judge it acceptable to defer given time/scope pressure — your call, weigh against how load-bearing this logic is (it drives the touch-only indicator's accuracy, which was itself a hard-won accessibility requirement from earlier in this build per §4a).
- Finding #5: this is the big one. Is a full architectural redesign in scope for a REWORK round, or does this get reported to Marcel as a real, novel accessibility gap requiring a decision (e.g., "should the scroll container always be keyboard-operable via arrow keys regardless of pointer capability, as an additive, non-visual fix")? Consider: a MINIMAL fix (making the scroll container itself keyboard-operable — tabIndex, onKeyDown wired to the same navigation function the visible arrows already use — regardless of pointer capability) is purely additive, doesn't touch the existing visual hover/touch CSS split at all, and directly closes the WCAG gap. Is that minimal fix authorizable this round, or does even that need Marcel's sign-off first given it changes a documented architectural decision (§4a/§4b)?

Give PASS or REWORK. If REWORK, be SPECIFIC and BOUNDED — name exactly which findings get fixed this round, which get deferred/reported, and if you authorize the keyboard-operability fix, describe its minimal required shape precisely enough that the Implementer can't over-build it into something bigger.

content.text: Root cause confirmed precisely: the Storybook decorator uses `maxWidth="320px"` with no explicit `width` — and for this component's fully percentage-based sizing chain (`width:100%` all the way down, by design, since it must fill an arbitrary grid cell in production), that decorator itself collapses to 8px in the single-image case. # Visual checkpoint — Step 4, `ZimmProductCardMedia`

This was the most involved step yet. The automated loop (Implementer → Tester → Orchestrator → Scorer) went two full rework rounds on real logic bugs, then my own visual check caught a third, separate defect that no automated test could have found.

## What the automated loop caught and fixed (rounds 1–2)

- **A real navigation bug**: if a card's image count shrinks while mounted (e.g. a colour-variant swap), clicking "Next" was a silent no-op on the first click. Fixed with the same clamp-on-shrink pattern already used by `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`.
- **A genuine WCAG 2.1.1 gap**: the arrows-vs-indicator split by pointer capability meant a device with no hover (a touchscreen with a keyboard attached, or a `hover:none` desktop browser) had **no way at all** to page a multi-image gallery via keyboard. Fixed by making the scroll container itself always keyboard-operable (arrow keys), independent of what's visually shown.
- Missing focus-ring styling on the arrow/close buttons, and zero test coverage on the single most important structural rule (arrows and the indicator must never both be interactive at once) — both closed.

## What I found at the visual checkpoint

Every single-image story (`Default` — the literal AC1 case — plus `WithBadge`, `WithRemoveButton`, `SingleImage`) rendered the entire card at **8×12 pixels** instead of filling the card. All 28 tests were green throughout, because jsdom never lays out real pixels — this was completely invisible to every automated gate.

Root cause: the Storybook decorator used `maxWidth="320px"` with no explicit `width`. This component's sizing is deliberately 100%-relative all the way down (it has to fill an arbitrary grid cell in the real PLP), and in that specific case a `maxWidth`-only box can resolve to its own shrink-to-fit size instead of stretching — confirmed live by setting `width` explicitly and watching it jump from 8×12 to a correct 320×480. **This is a story-file bug, not a component bug** — a real CSS Grid cell (SFCC-80, not built yet) always provides a definite width, so I'm confident this doesn't recur in production, but it's exactly the kind of thing that's worth ten seconds in a browser rather than trusting green tests alone.

## For your own check

**URL:** `http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/commerce-zimmproductcardmedia--multiple-images`

| Story | What to look for |
|---|---|
| `Default` | Card fills the ~320px canvas at a 2:3 ratio, not a sliver |

| `With remove button (wishlist)` | ✕ button sits flush top-right of the card, not cut off |
| `With Badge` | Badge sits top-left, and it should **not** react to hover or look clickable (that's deliberate — badges are display-only per SPR-16) |

**What would indicate a defect:** any story rendering as a thin sliver instead of a full card; arrows and the touch position-indicator both visible at once; a focus ring that's cut off or missing on the arrows/close button/scroll region.

Straight answer: **it's made up.** Let me be precise about which part is and isn't grounded in Figma.

## What's real

The **position and footprint** of the badge slot — top-left, `78×48` min-area — comes from a real node: `40002742:46322` ("Image Group / Size=Large"), whose `Tag` frame sits at `(0,0)`, `78×48`, containing a `touchContainer` at `(24,12)` sized `30×24` holding a `Label`. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `tag` recipe part (`position:absolute, top:0, left:0, minWidth:78px, minHeight:48px`) is a direct citation of that.

## What's invented

The actual **pill you see** in that story — dark fill, white "Exclusive" text, rounded padding — is a placeholder I wrote for demo purposes. It's not pulled from either badge node we resolved:

- `Badge` (`40001471:20752`, States Primary/Hover, 33×15) — I confirmed this node **exists** and confirmed the real card's `Tag` slot does **not** instance it (its child is a raw `Label` text node, not a `Badge` instance). But I never actually fetched what `State=Primary` looks like — I resolved its ID and scope status, not its visual design.
- `Stock Status Badge` (`40001796:7041`) — out of scope, Marcel's call, unrelated to this anyway.

So the honest state is: I know the **slot** is real, I know one candidate badge **component exists but isn't what the card uses**, and I have **no confirmed source at all** for what should render inside — the card's own `Tag` child is just an unstyled text label with no Chakra/token spec attached to it in Figma.

The component code reflects this correctly — `badge` is typed `React.ReactNode`, and `ZimmProductCardMedia` deliberately doesn't style it, only positions it. But the *story* needed something to show, and what it shows is a placeholder passing as a plausible design, which is exactly the kind of thing worth catching before it ships. Nobody should look at that story and think "that's the badge design."

Want me to pull `40001471:20751` (`Badge / State=Primary`) now and see what it actually looks like, in case that's closer to truth than a made-up pill — or flag this as an open item for Kiera since even the real `Badge` component isn't confirmed as what the card is meant to use?

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx

Do not touch any file outside this list — in particular do NOT touch `zimmSlideIndicator/`, `zimmSizeChip*/`, `zimmProductPrice/`, or `zimmProductCardMedia/` (all already committed from prior steps).

## CRITICAL — two things from the original plan are now WRONG, read this before writing anything
1. **No badge.** An earlier version of this plan moved a badge slot into `ZimmProductCardMedia` (Step 4). That slot has since been **removed entirely** — Marcel confirmed no design requires a badge on the image, and it was not moved anywhere else. **Do not build a badge slot in this component either.** This component has no `badge` prop, no badge rendering, nothing. The SFCC-236 AC's mention of "badge" for PLP/Wishlist is currently unbuilt anywhere in this codebase — that's a known, accepted gap, not something for you to fill by guessing a home for it.
2. **No remove/close button.** The wishlist remove ('x') CTA lives entirely in `ZimmProductCardMedia` (the `close` overlay, built in Step 4) — it is positioned on the image, not in this text-content component. Do not add `onRemove`/`removeLabel` props or any remove-button rendering here.

## Read these exemplars FIRST, in full, before writing anything
1. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` and `.css.ts` (Step 4, just committed) — for the current, correct shape of this component family: `data-card-slot` contract comments, how `useMultiStyleConfig` is called, `chakra.*`/`__css` usage, `defineMessages`/`useIntl` pattern, JSDoc style.
2. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductName/index.tsx` — you will compose this atom for the product name/heading.
3. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx` — you will compose this atom for price, **passing `isLive={false}`** (see below).
4. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/index.tsx` and its sibling `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/index.tsx` (Step 2, already committed) — you will compose `ZimmSizeChipGroup` for the size-picker slot.
5. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductMeta/index.tsx` — an existing molecule that composes multiple product-info atoms together; useful as a second reference for how this codebase composes atoms into a text-block molecule (distinct from the image-focused `zimmProductCardMedia` reference above).

## Design source (verified Figma — do not re-derive)
`Card-content` component set, node `40002109:26908` (Desktop `40002109:26906` / Mobile `40002163:37103`). Verified internal structure of the Desktop variant:
```
Content(40,32,208x138)
  > Frame(208x82)
      > Product name and attributes(208x49)
          > Product name and icons(208x25)
              > Card heading instance (176x25)   <- product name
              > Icons(184,0,24x24) > touchContainer(24x24) > Icon_bag instance(4,4,16x16)  <- bag button
          > Attributes(0,41,208x8)
              > Colour text (53x8)
              > Size text (43x8)
      > Price text (0,73,208x9)
      > Size Selector instance (0,106,208x28, hidden=true)  <- hidden by default, reveals on hover (organism's job, Step 6)
  > Link instance (0,114,57x24)
```
**Confirmed in Figma directly (from an earlier resolution in this build): it's a BAG icon (`Icon_bag`), not a wishlist star** — SPR-14/SPR-15 (the signed-off functional requirements) were amended from wishlist to cart/bag, and this matches. Do not build a wishlist heart here.

## Component contract
Props — this component takes **booleans/values derived from the organism's variation logic (Step 6, not built yet)**, never a `variation` string literal, so it never needs to know variation names:
```ts
type ZimmProductCardContentProps = {
  name: string;
  headingLevel: 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4'; // matches ZimmProductName's own headingLevel-shaped prop — check its exact type and reuse/match it, don't invent a parallel shape
  href: string; // the name renders as a link to the PDP
  currentPrice?: string;
  originalPrice?: string;
  isPriceLoading?: boolean; // passthrough to ZimmProductPrice's own isLoading

  showAttributes: boolean; // wishlist only, per the organism's VARIATION_CONFIG (not built yet — this component just takes the boolean)
  colour?: string; // rendered only when showAttributes is true
  size?: string;   // rendered only when showAttributes is true

  showBag: boolean;
  isUnavailable?: boolean; // disables the bag button when true
  onAddToBag?: () => void;

  showSizeChips: boolean; // PLP only, per the organism's config

Guard clause + native `disabled` both block `onAddToBag` (`index.tsx:184,190-191`); proven with a `fireEvent.click` that bypasses React's synthetic handler entirely (`index.test.tsx:117-130`).

Not a Hard-Rule-12 situation either: nothing was ambiguous, the sketch was simply factually wrong against already-shipped code.

**c) `chakra(RouteLink)` built directly in this molecule.** Matches an existing, already-established codebase idiom exactly: `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:3-11` does the identical `chakra(RouteLink)` construction for the identical reason, and Content's own comment (`index.tsx:27-30`) cites it directly. None of the three rises to scope creep.

### 4. Cross-tier check

CODEOWNERS confirms: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` → both squads (`CODEOWNERS:176`), `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → both squads (`CODEOWNERS:186`), `overrides/app/theme/components/` → Tier 2 + Tier 1 approvers (`CODEOWNERS:117`). ```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/zimmProductCardContent.css.ts

## Fix 1 — name/bag-icon row vertical alignment
File: `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`, the `nameRow` part.

Currently: `alignItems: 'flex-start'`.

Figma ground truth (pulled directly via `get_design_context` on node `40002163:41441`, the real assembled Desktop/Default/PLP-PDP card — not just the standalone documentation set): the "Card heading" (name) element resolves to a taller effective box than the "Icons"/`touchContainer` (bag icon) element, because of their different internal padding (name: 8px padding around 16px line-height ≈ 32px tall; icon: 4px padding around a 16px icon = 24px tall). With the row's `alignItems` set to `flex-start`, these two different-height children top-align, producing a visible ~4px vertical offset between the icon's optical centre and the name text's optical centre — this is exactly the visual misalignment that was spotted in the live Storybook render.

Change `nameRow`'s `alignItems` from `'flex-start'` to `'center'`. This vertically centers both children regardless of their differing internal padding, which is the correct, robust way to align a text label against an icon button of a different height in a horizontal flex row — and matches what the design visually shows (name and icon centred together), even though Figma's own auto-generated code approximation happens to specify `items-start` at the container level (Figma's codegen for auto-layout doesn't always perfectly capture visual centering achieved via matching padding in the original design tool).

Update the existing comment above `nameRow` (currently explaining the `gap` value) to also note why `alignItems: 'center'` is used, citing this reasoning briefly.

## Fix 2 — notify-me control: wrong copy, wrong colour token, wrong/placeholder spacing
This control had NO real Figma grounding when originally built — it was inferred from the Jira AC's prose ("a notify me link appears on hover"). It has since been found in the actual design: node `40002163:41468` (Desktop, Hover, PLP/PDP, Unavailable=True — the exact state the AC describes), which shows the real control clearly. Pulled directly via `get_design_context` on that node:

**Real copy:** the literal text is **"NOTIFY ME"** (all-caps, two words) — not "Notify me when back in stock". The extra phrase was invented; remove it entirely.

**Real component identity:** in Figma, this is not a bespoke button — it's an instance of the same generic `CTA/Link` atom used elsewhere in this component set (node `40001908:28374`/`40001908:28368`, 57×24), just with contextual text swapped to "NOTIFY ME" in this state. Its styling per the design-context pull:
- Text style: Figma names it `Default/Link-sm` (font-size `brand/font/size/300` ≈12px, weight 500/bold, line-height `brand/font/lineheight/350`, letter-spacing `brand/font/letterspacing/negative-100`) — this maps to this codebase's own `textStyle: 'linkSm'`, which is **already what the recipe currently uses** — do not change the `textStyle` value, it was already correct.
- **Colour: `alias/color/link/default`** (a real, distinct semantic token in Figma) — **NOT** `text/default`, even though both happen to resolve to the same hex (`#191919`) in this palette. The current recipe uses `color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)'`, which is the wrong semantic category — a real `--zimm-color-link-default` token already exists in this codebase (`overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:79`). Change the colour to `var(--zimm-color-link-default)`.
- Underline: the Figma text carries a genuine underline (`underline decoration-from-font`) — check whether the current `textStyle: 'linkSm'` already includes underline styling (it likely does, since it's a link text style) by reading `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts`'s `linkSm` definition; if it doesn't already underline, that's a separate, larger finding to report rather than hack around here (do not add an ad-hoc `textDecoration` override to work around a textStyle that's supposed to already handle this — report it instead if you find a mismatch).

**Real spacing:** the design-context pull shows the "Content" wrapper (the flex column holding name-block, price, and this notify-me link when present) applies a **uniform 24px gap** (`var(--alias/space/600, 24px)`) between ALL of its direct children — including between price and this notify-me link. This is the exact same `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` token already used elsewhere in this same recipe for the name-block-to-price gap. The current recipe's `notifyMeButton.marginTop` uses `var(--zimm-scale-m)` (16px) with a comment saying it's "a placeholder — no Figma spec exists... pending UI-designer sign-off." That comment is now out of date — a real, confirmed value exists. Change `marginTop` to `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` and update/remove the "no spec exists, placeholder" comment to instead cite the real source (the same `Content` wrapper's uniform 24px gap, node `40002163:41470`, confirmed via `get_design_context`).

**In `index.tsx`:** change the `notifyMe` message's `defaultMessage` from `'Notify me when back in stock'` to `'Notify me'` — wait, check the EXACT casing Figma shows: the raw text node is `"NOTIFY ME"` in all-caps. Check how this codebase's other all-caps-looking UI text is actually authored — e.g. does `ZimmProductName`'s "Product Name" or the Tag's "LABEL" get authored as normal-case text with a CSS `text-transform: uppercase` applied by the textStyle (which is the pattern I'd expect, since raw copy should stay sentence-case/normal-case for i18n and accessibility reasons, with visual capitalisation handled purely by CSS) — read `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts`'s `linkSm` definition to check if it already applies `textTransform: 'uppercase'` or similar. If `linkSm` already visually uppercases its text via CSS, author the `defaultMessage` as normal sentence case (`'Notify me'`) and let the textStyle handle the visual caps — do NOT hardcode literal `'NOTIFY ME'` as the translatable string (that would be wrong for i18n — a translator should translate "Notify me", not a pre-capitalised string). If `linkSm` does NOT already uppercase, report this as a finding rather than deciding unilaterally which layer should own the capitalisation.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts
npx vitest run overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts
npx eslint overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
npm run test
```
All must be clean/green. Confirm via `git status --porcelain` that only `zimmProductCardContent/` files (and possibly the pre-existing unchanged `theme/components/index.ts` diff) show any change — nothing else. Do NOT stage or commit.

Report exactly what changed (before/after for each of the two fixes), what you found when checking `linkSm`'s definition for underline/uppercase handling (and what you did as a result), and confirm all verification commands pass.

Confirmed precisely — name centre (28px) and bag icon centre (28px) now match exactly. Alignment fixed.

# Step 5 checkpoint — round 2, everything now traced to a real spec

Per your directive, here's everything grounded, with sources:

## Fixed and verified

| Issue | Was | Now | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name/bag alignment | `alignItems: flex-start` (icon and text off by 4px — confirmed both by your eye and by DOM math: name box ~32px vs icon box 24px) | `alignItems: center` | Node `40002163:41441`, verified: both now centre at y=28px exactly |
| Notify-me copy | "Notify me when back in stock" (invented) | "Notify me" | Node `40002163:41468` — real text is literally "NOTIFY ME" |
| Notify-me colour | `--zimm-color-text-default` (wrong category) | `--zimm-color-link-default` | Figma names it `alias/color/link/default`; confirmed this token already exists in `zimmTokens.ts:79` |
| Notify-me spacing | `--zimm-scale-m` (16px, flagged "placeholder pending sign-off") | `--zimm-scale-xl` (24px) | Node `40002163:41470` — the same uniform 24px gap already used elsewhere in this recipe, not a new value |

## Two things that need your eyes, not my judgement

**1. Real design-system bug found, not touched (Tier 1).** `linkSm` (`theme/foundation/typography.ts`) uses `textTransform: 'capitalize'`. Every other caps-styled text in this codebase (e.g. `ZimmProductName`'s style) uses `'uppercase'`. Figma's "NOTIFY ME" is genuinely all-caps. Confirmed visually: it currently renders **"Notify Me"**, not "NOTIFY ME". I didn't touch `typography.ts` — that's yours or the UI designer's call, not something to silently patch from inside a molecule.

**2. AC vs. design mismatch.** The Jira AC says the notify-me link appears "**instead of** price." The actual Figma node (`40002163:41468`) shows **both together** — $850 stays visible, "NOTIFY ME" appears below it. I built to the design, not the AC text, but flagging the contradiction since nobody's reconciled it yet.

Both resolved during this session, already answered by you: the "LABEL" tag placeholder in the real card instance was confirmed as Figma noise, not a reversal of the badge removal.

All gates green (51 files/792 tests), nothing outside `zimmProductCardContent/` touched. Going forward I'll pull the real Figma node for every visual claim before it ships, not after you catch it.

**No dual-case variant needed.** `linkSm` has exactly one real consumer anywhere in this codebase — the notify-me link. There's no second use case pulling it toward Title Case, so a variant would be pure speculative engineering for a need that doesn't exist. Per the "no premature abstraction" rule: keep it as the single corrected value (`uppercase`), and if a genuine Title-Case consumer shows up later, that's the point to add a second named style or a variant — backed by a real requirement, not in anticipation of one.

| **Process issue** | The Implementer I dispatched for the alignment/notify-me fixes appears to have made this exact edit, then told me it hadn't. Both files were touched 13 seconds apart. Its self-report was wrong on this specific point — worth knowing, since I was relying on that report. |

content: why are we using linkSm for this instead of the zimm one?

message.content: why are we using linkSm for this instead of the zimm one?

content.text:
Because it's the project's documented, mandatory mechanism for text — not a preference I made up. From `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s styling hierarchy (point 1): *"`textStyle` prop for anything textual... never a raw `fontSize`."* And separately, `.zimm-*` global classes are explicitly scoped to a different job:

> *"`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive, massively-reused treatments... where there's no interactive state to lose."*

The notify-me link isn't that — it's an interactive control with its own `_focusVisible` ring, applied via the same recipe object right next to `textStyle: 'linkSm'`. If it used `className="zimm-text-link-sm"` instead, the text styling would live in one system (a raw CSS class) while the focus ring lives in another (Chakra's `__css`) — exactly the split-surface anti-pattern `overrideStyling.md`'s "One canonical styling surface per component type" section warns against:

> *"A static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class 'mirror' is structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing with the real theme config over time."*

That's not theoretical here — it's exactly what just happened. `.zimm-text-link-sm` **had** drifted out of sync with `linkSm` until five minutes ago. If the component had been built against the `.zimm-*` class instead of the `textStyle`, it would have shipped the stale `capitalize` value, and there'd have been no test catching it — the collision-guard test only exists to check the two surfaces *agree*, not to make either one safe to build against directly.

One more practical point: `overrideStyling.md`'s own "Follow-up work" section notes the `.zimm-*` registry has *"near zero adoption... none have a real consumer anywhere in the app today except one Storybook demo."* They're a 1:1 port of the Handover spec, kept for a future static/non-Chakra use case that hasn't materialized — not the live path for anything built through `useMultiStyleConfig`, which is how every component in this entire build (this one included) is styled.

content.text:
Not a stylistic call — I looked for evidence of two real, distinct design tokens and found none. Here's the actual reasoning:

**`linkSm` maps 1:1 to a single named Handover style.** Per `overrideStyling.md`: *"All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`."* The comment in the code names it explicitly — `ZIM/Link-sm`.
